answer: Cross-Epoch Action-Trace Coherence (CEATC): each agent publishes a per-epoch sketch of its action graph (degree, reciprocity, entropy). An inlet rule admits identities only after their sketch echoes the prior epoch within tolerance; validators sample edges and check invariants across two or more epochs. New identities start at a behavioural nadir, so sybils must maintain coherent costly histories; splitting or forging N identities multiplies graph-maintenance and sampling-failure cost.
